transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um… mostly it’s this constant tension. My shoulders and neck are clenched pretty much all day, like I’m bracing for something at work that never actually happens. By evening my jaw aches, and it’s gotten to where I can barely enjoy playing guitar. That’s what finally made me come in.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, like work, relationships, or other responsibilities, even when there isn’t a clear reason to be concerned?

Yeah… I do. It jumps around a lot. Work stuff, mostly—whether I’ll ever get hired again, if parents think badly of me now. Then it turns into retirement, money… and sometimes even some small mistake in a story-time activity, like maybe that means I shouldn’t be trusted with kids. I know that sounds like a lot.
Do you feel like your worrying is something you can’t really control or turn off, even when you try?

Yeah… it’s hard to shut it off. I’ll try to do something sensible, like make a list, or pray, or go weed the garden—just focus on the next step. But then one worry kind of hands it off to the next one, and before I know it I’ve lost half the afternoon.
Do you ever feel physically restless, like you can’t sit still or relax, even when you want to?
I’m not sure. I mean… I don’t think of it as not being able to sit still exactly. I just don’t really feel relaxed much.
Do you often feel tired or run down, even if you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I haven’t really kept track of it. I wouldn’t say I’m doing heavy physical stuff, but… yeah, I can feel kind of worn out. Hard to say how much of that is anything, though.
Do you find it hard to focus or concentrate on tasks, like reading or following a conversation, because your mind feels overwhelmed or distracted?

Yeah… sometimes. If I’m filling out applications, or even just trying to plan a simple lesson, I’ll realize I’ve read the same paragraph over and over. My mind keeps jumping to, you know, what the administrator might think, or whether I missed some important detail. It makes it hard to stay with the task.
Do you find that your worrying happens more days than not and has been going on like this for at least six months?
Yeah… more days than not, I think. It’s been going on for a while now — about a year and a couple months, since I was fired from the preschool.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, even when you’re tired?

Yeah… most nights, I think. I’ll be tired, but then I’m just lying there going over things — interviews, bills, forms I need to deal with. It can take hours. And sometimes I wake up around four already tense, like I’m already trying to figure out what’s going to go wrong.

Do you find that your anxiety is not just about specific events like job interviews or bills, but more about a general sense that things could go wrong in many different areas of your life, even when there’s no clear reason?

Yeah… it’s not just one thing. My mind kind of circles around all of it — whether I’ll ever get hired again, whether parents think badly of me now, whether I’ve messed up my retirement somehow. Even small things, like if I made a mistake in a story-time activity, I start thinking maybe that means I shouldn’t be trusted with kids. It… gets bigger than the situation, I guess.
Have you noticed that these symptoms, like the tension in your body and trouble focusing, are worse during times of stress, or do they seem to be present even when things are calm?

It’s worse when I’m stressed, yeah… but honestly it doesn’t really go away when things are quiet either. My shoulders and neck just stay clenched most of the day, like I’m bracing for something. By evening my jaw aches, and I can’t even really enjoy playing guitar.
Do these symptoms interfere with your ability to function in your daily life, like doing your job, taking care of responsibilities, or enjoying time with others?

Yeah… it does. I don’t like admitting that, but I’ve missed application deadlines, and in interviews I sort of freeze or stumble through things. I’ve stopped volunteering for story-time unless someone else is doing the planning part. So… it’s making it hard to get back into a classroom in any dependable way.
